children: Overview
US airline's Q3 revenue rose 14% yr/yr, driven by premium and loyalty growth
Company posted Q3 net loss due to elevated fuel costs
Announced intent to join Atlantic and Pacific Joint International Businesses with oneworld partners
Outlook
Alaska Air expects Q4 capacity to grow 1% to 1.5% year-over-year
Company sees Q4 unit revenue up low double digits year-over-year
Alaska Air forecasts Q4 adjusted loss per share of $2.50 to $2.00
Result Drivers
ELEVATED FUEL COSTS - Co said higher fuel prices drove Q3 net loss and reduced profitability
PREMIUM AND LOYALTY GROWTH - Premium revenue grew 25% and loyalty program cash remuneration rose 21% yr/yr, contributing to revenue growth
INTERNATIONAL EXPANSION - Co expanded international network with new routes to Paris, Athens, Osaka and Papeete, supporting capacity and revenue growth
